author: simonabler
body:
Prevents the coder↔reviewer loop from spinning indefinitely by implementing three deterministic exit conditions (in priority order):

1. Max rework cycles (hard ceiling) → ESCALATE_TESTING  [existing]
2. Diff-delta convergence: if SequenceMatcher ratio of successive git diffs >= 0.97 after ≥2 rework cycles → ESCALATE_CONVERGENCE → tester. The coder is no longer making meaningful changes; the reviewer is going in circles. Hand off to the objective tester.
3. Second+ rework cycle → REWORK_VIA_TESTER: run tester before sending back to coder so a deterministic pass/fail can short-circuit further subjective reviewer loops.
4. First rework → CODING (fast path, no tester overhead).

Implementation:
- TodoItem.last_coder_diff: git diff HEAD snapshot stored by coder after each pass, used by _check_convergence on the next cycle.
- GraphState.convergence_detected: surfaced to UI/logs for visibility.
- _check_convergence(): difflib.SequenceMatcher comparison helper.

Addresses: STRAT-OC-003b (feedback loop without convergence check)

Tests: 20 new tests in tests/test_convergence.py covering _check_convergence unit tests and all four peer_review routing paths.

author: lautaropetaccio
body:
Sentry is reporting `JS idle timeout exceeded` errors on `/auth/login`. These errors originate entirely from third-party scripts (Segment, Safary, Reddit pixel, ID5, etc.) — not from application code. The breadcrumbs show repeated "Still loading scripts..." logs every ~250ms from third-party script initialization, followed by the idle timeout error. These are not actionable and add noise to the Sentry dashboard.

The exact string "JS idle timeout exceeded" does not exist in the Sentry SDK itself — it is thrown by one of the third-party scripts and merely captured by Sentry's `sentryWrapped` handler.

## How

Added a filter in `beforeSend` (`src/modules/analytics/sentry.ts`) that drops events matching both conditions:

1. The exception message contains "idle timeout exceeded"
2. **All** stack frames are non-app code (`!frame.in_app`) — meaning the error originated entirely from third-party scripts

This ensures that if application code ever throws a similar error, it will still be reported.

### FE-37: Groups page (`src/app/dashboard/groups/page.tsx`)

### Supporting: edit/create pages

Tested full flow on tournament `300420ff-d9e3-4238-8c87-0b993e4ee103`:

body:
### Motivation
- Improve extraction and display of monster descriptions and actions from external HTML sources while preserving basic formatting and safe links.
- Reduce false negatives when scraping varied site structures by better content root detection and pruning noisy elements.
- Prevent unsafe hrefs and inline scripts by sanitizing rich HTML before rendering in the sheet.

### Description
- Added comprehensive HTML parsing and sanitization utilities: `sanitizeMonsterRichHtml`, `normalizeMonsterHref`, `linkifyMonsterTextNodes`, and `pruneMonsterHtmlDocument` to clean and safe-ify incoming HTML content.
- Implemented structured content extraction with `findBestMonsterContentRoot`, `getMonsterBlockNodes`, `extractMonsterRichEntryFromBlock`, and `parseMonsterStructuredContent` to identify description, main body, traits, actions, bonus actions, reactions, and legendary actions as HTML and text.
- Extended data model and normalization: `normalizeMonsterEntries` now preserves `html` alongside `text`, parse functions populate `description_html` and `main_body_html`, and `parseMonsterText` merges structured results into `data` when available.
- Updated rendering and styles to support sanitized HTML output: `renderEntries`, `renderMainTraitPanels`, and new `renderMainSectionPanels` now prefer `entry.html` or `description_html`/`main_body_html` when present, and CSS adjusted for lists and links.

## Summary

Adds Edge browser support for automatic cookie extraction. Edge uses Chromium's cookie store format, and the `kooky` library already has an `edge` module — this just imports it.

## Changes

- `cookies.go`: Import `github.com/browserutils/kooky/browser/edge`
- `cookies.go`: Update error message to mention Edge
- `README.md`: Add Edge to browser support table

## Testing

Tested on macOS with Edge as primary browser — successfully extracts cookies and queries Zendesk tickets. Edge cookies are checked in Phase 2 alongside Safari and Chrome via kooky's registered finders.

## Why

Edge is Chromium-based and widely used (especially in enterprise environments where GitHub support is most needed). Users with Edge as their primary browser couldn't use automatic cookie extraction and had to manually set `ZENDESK_COOKIE`.

## Summary

Hardens the Stacks API client for production reliability:

- **Request timeout** — 10s AbortController timeout prevents hanging requests on slow networks
- **Retry-After header** — respects server-requested backoff delay instead of fixed exponential backoff
- **Request deduplication** — concurrent identical requests within 200ms share a single in-flight promise

## Changes

- `src/lib/stacks-api.ts` — Timeout via AbortController, Retry-After parsing, abort error handling
- `src/lib/request-cache.ts` — NEW deduplication utility with auto-eviction
- `src/lib/index.ts` — Barrel export for deduplicatedFetch

## Test plan

- Slow network: requests timeout after 10s instead of hanging indefinitely
- Rate limited (429): respects Retry-After header delay
- Mount multiple components using same query → only one network request fires

author: jjrawlins
body:
## Summary

- **`delete_episode` MCP tool**: Exposes the existing `DeleteEpisode` store method as an MCP tool, allowing clients to permanently remove episodes. Previously only available via REST API. Description guides users toward soft-delete (`update_episode` with `expired_at`) when recovery may be needed.

- **Keyword search ILIKE fallback**: DuckDB FTS strips pure numeric tokens during indexing, so keyword searches for account IDs, ticket numbers, and other numeric identifiers returned empty. When keyword mode returns no BM25 results, the search now falls back to `ILIKE` content matching. The fallback only triggers when BM25 finds nothing — normal text queries still use BM25 ranking. All standard filters (group_id, tags, temporal, expired) are applied to fallback results.

## Breaking changes

None. Existing search behavior is unchanged — the fallback only activates when BM25 returns zero results in keyword mode.

## Test plan

- [x] All existing tests pass unchanged
- [x] `TestSearchKeywordNumericFallback/numeric_account_ID_found_via_fallback` — pure numeric query finds episode via ILIKE
- [x] `TestSearchKeywordNumericFallback/text_keywords_still_use_BM25_not_fallback` — text queries use BM25, fallback doesn't interfere
- [x] `TestSearchKeywordNumericFallback/fallback_respects_group_filter` — group_id filter applied to fallback results
- [x] Live tested standalone (PR branch only, no other PRs): numeric keyword found correct episode, delete_episode created and deleted test episode
- [x] Live tested during real migration workflow: delete_episode cleaned up misplaced episodes, numeric keyword fallback found episodes by AWS account ID

author: enkechen-panw
body:
rib_route_match_ctx() matches a returning dplane result back to the correct route_entry.  For ZEBRA_ROUTE_STATIC it narrowed the match using both distance and tag.  However, tag is an attribute of the route_entry, not part of its identity — a tag change modifies the route_entry in place without creating a new one.

Including tag in the match creates a race: if a tag update arrives and modifies re->tag before a pending dplane result is processed, the stored re->tag no longer matches the tag captured in the dplane context, and the correct route_entry is not found.

Since distance alone is sufficient to identify a ZEBRA_ROUTE_STATIC route_entry (before metric is introduced as a key), remove the tag comparison.

author: galo2099
body:
### Motivation
- Rendering the championship table executed a `next_game` lookup per team which caused an N+1 query pattern and extra DB round-trips while building the popup header. 
- The change aims to fetch all upcoming games for the phase/team set in one query and map each team to its nearest upcoming match to reduce DB queries and improve rendering performance.

### Description
- Added helper `next_games_by_team(phase, team_ids, start_date = Date.today)` in `app/helpers/championship_helper.rb` which performs a single SQL query, eager-loads `:home` and `:away`, orders by `date, id`, and returns a hash mapping team id to its next `Game`.
- Removed the per-team method `TeamCampaign#next_game` to avoid per-row queries (previously in `app/helpers/championship_helper.rb`).

author: ada-x64
body:
## Summary

Migrate bzip2 CI from raw `make -f Makefile.nanvix` invocations to the `./z` lifecycle powered by `nanvix-zutil` v0.2.2. This aligns bzip2 with the zlib reference implementation and improves SHA consistency across matrix builds.

## Changes

### Commit 1: `z` bootstrap and `.nanvix/z.py`
- **`z`** — Bash bootstrap script (identical to the zutils v0.2.2 template, SHA256-pinned wheel install)
- **`.nanvix/z.py`** — `Bzip2Build(ZScript)` class wrapping `Makefile.nanvix` with `setup`/`build`/`test`/`release`/`clean` lifecycle hooks
- **`.gitignore`** — Exclude `.nanvix/` runtime state (venv, cache, sysroot, buildroot, env.json) and `dist/` while keeping `.nanvix/z.py` tracked
- Deleted `bzip2.elf` (1.5 MB binary that was accidentally committed)

### Commit 2: CI workflow migration
- Replace `get-nanvix-info` (downloaded all release artifacts to extract SHA from filenames) with a lightweight `resolve-nanvix-info` job that queries the GitHub API once
- Replace 6 manual `make` steps with 4 `./z` commands (`setup`, `build`, `test`, `release`)
- Pin all build matrix jobs to the resolved SHA via `NANVIX_TAG`, preventing race windows where a mid-workflow Nanvix release could cause matrix jobs to build against different sysroots
- Add failure log collection and upload steps
- Simplify release job by consuming `resolve-nanvix-info` outputs directly

### Commit 3: Fix `clean()` method
- Call `make` directly in `clean()` instead of routing through `_make_args()`, which would crash if `./z setup` hadn't been run (the Makefile already gates its `NANVIX_HOME` check with `ifneq ($(MAKECMDGOALS),clean)`)

## Improvement over zlib

The `resolve-nanvix-info` + `NANVIX_TAG` pinning approach is architecturally better than zlib's current workflow, where the Nanvix SHA is resolved at release time after all builds complete. This closes a race window and should be backported to zlib as a follow-up.

## Testing

- CI will validate end-to-end on all 5 matrix configurations (hyperlight/microvm × multi-process/single-process/standalone)

(Moved from #26)

author: andrewgazelka
body: ## Release notes summary ### MCP: Auto-promote long-running evaluations to background jobs Evaluations that take longer than 10 seconds, or are cancelled by the client, are automatically promoted to background jobs instead of being discarded. Their results are delivered to job 0's mailbox, where they can be retrieved using `job recv`. These promoted jobs appear in `job list` with descriptions like `mcp: `, and they can be terminated using `job kill`. The timeout for this behavior can be configured through the `$env.NU_MCP_PROMOTE_AFTER` setting. ## Example ``` Client → evaluate("http get https://slow-api.com/data | to json") # After 10s, server auto-promotes: Server → error: "Operation promoted to background job (id: 1)..." # Client can discover and retrieve: Client → evaluate("job list") Client → evaluate("job recv --timeout 60sec") ``` ## Test plan - [x] Existing tests pass (`cargo test -p nu-mcp`) - [x] `test_cancellation_promotes_to_background_job` — verifies promotion message and state isolation - [x] Manual: slow eval auto-promotes after 10s, result retrievable via `job recv`

body:
### Motivation

- Unify the device/topic model so local Mosquitto and Yandex use the same `$devices/{mqtt_user}` commands/events convention.  
- Modernize and harden dynamic-security interactions by moving to the `$CONTROL/dynamic-security/v1` control/response API and improving error/timeout handling.  
- Align ESP firmware behavior and registration checks with the unified topic model and ensure credentials consistency between DB/dynsec and device.  

### Description

- Backend: updated `backend/src/mqtt/providers/local.js` to require `mqtt`, add broader env var fallbacks, and introduce `DYNSEC_CONTROL_TOPIC`, `DYNSEC_RESPONSE_TOPIC`, and a configurable `DYNSEC_TIMEOUT_MS`.  
- Backend: added parsing for `$devices/{mqtt_user}/events` in `parseMessage`, resolving `mqtt_user` → `device_id` via DB lookup, and returning unified `{ deviceId, online, fw, relays }`.  
- Backend: replaced `_dynsecSend` with `_dynsecCommand` to send single commands, subscribe only to the response topic, include timeouts, result validation, and a helper `_isIgnorableDynsecError`; createClient now sets password and textname atomically and ACLs include new `$devices/...` topics while keeping legacy topics for backward compatibility.  
- Backend: simplified `registerDevice` and `deleteDevice` flow to use the new command helper and improved error handling/logging.  
- ESP firmware: changed topic templates in `janitor-esp/config.h` to `DEVICE_CMD_TMPL`/`DEVICE_EVENTS_TMPL` based on `$devices/%s/...`, tightened `DeviceConfig::isRegistered()` to require `mqtt_pass`, and adjusted status printing.  
- ESP firmware: updated `janitor-esp.ino` and `janitor-esp/mqtt_mgr.h` to use `$devices/{mqtt_user}/commands` for subscriptions and `$devices/{mqtt_user}/events` for LWT/online/changes publishing, simplified topic selection logic, and updated logs.  

### Testing

- Ran backend automated tests with `npm test`, which completed successfully.  
- Performed an integration smoke test against a local Mosquitto with dynsec: device registration via the new dynsec flow and a commands/events roundtrip both succeeded.  
- Compiled the ESP firmware with the current build configuration (Arduino/PlatformIO) to verify no compilation regressions, and the build succeeded.

author: kltm
body:
## Summary

Replaces the manual gcloud workflow with Terraform infrastructure-as-code and adds a real-time spend estimator to bridge GCP's 12-24h billing data lag.

### Terraform automation (`terraform/`)
- All GCP resources as HCL: service accounts, IAM bindings, APIs, Pub/Sub, Cloud Run, Cloud Scheduler, billing budget
- Self-documenting `variables.tf` — the primary configuration reference
- `resource_prefix` variable (default: `tf`) so Terraform-managed resources coexist with manual ones
- Local-only state with guidance on transfer and `terraform import`
- Tested end-to-end against a live GCP project

### Real-time spend estimation (flux estimator)
- Queries `publisher/online_serving/token_count` from Cloud Monitoring every 5 minutes
- Per-model pricing for 20 models (Claude Opus/Sonnet/Haiku + Gemini families)
- Cache-aware: reads at 0.1x, writes at 1.25-2x base input price
- 10% regional endpoint premium applied by default (configurable)
- Falls back to call counting if token metrics unavailable
- `ENFORCEMENT_TOLERANCE` scalar (0.8=early cutoff, 1.0=exact, 1.2=tolerant)
- Pricing table approach adapted from [microbiomedata/nmdc-metadata-suggestor-ai-tool](https://github.com/microbiomedata/nmdc-metadata-suggestor-ai-tool)

### Documentation
- `CLAUDE.md` — Project context, onboarding, pricing maintenance checklist
- `README.md` — Architecture, two enforcement mechanisms explained with diagrams, budget limit section
- `docs/MANUAL_STEPS.md` — The 5 steps that cannot be automated
- `.gitignore` — Blocks credentials, state files, tfvars

### Safety properties
- `SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL` references consumer SA by construction — can't target admin SA
- Pub/Sub invoker IAM binding is a separate Terraform resource — survives Cloud Run redeployments
- No secrets in Terraform state (JSON key creation is manual)
- No real project IDs, SA emails, or credentials in any committed file
- Budget scopes to all services (Claude charges bill under marketplace, not "Vertex AI")

## Commits

1. **Initial Terraform scaffolding** — full IaC for all GCP resources
2. **Fixes from live testing** — billing budget API, resource prefix, expanded CLAUDE.md
3. **Auth correction** — Owner role not required (service account with sufficient roles works)
4. **Monitoring output + lock file** — usage check command, pinned provider version
5. **Flux estimator v1** — call-count based real-time spend estimation
6. **README rewrite** — plain-language explanation with diagrams for developer clarity
7. **Token-based estimator** — switched to publisher/online_serving/token_count metric with per-model pricing and cache awareness
8. **Pricing update** — added claude-sonnet-4-6 and newer Gemini models
9. **Regional premium** — 10% surcharge for non-global endpoints, pricing maintenance docs

## Test plan

- [x] `terraform init && terraform plan && terraform apply` against live GCP project
- [x] Container builds and deploys to Cloud Run
- [x] Pub/Sub -> Cloud Run pipeline: 200 response, keys disabled
- [x] Key re-enable and re-disable cycle verified
- [x] Cloud Monitoring response_count metrics confirmed for Vertex AI calls
- [x] Budget change ($5 -> $1) applied via `terraform apply` (single resource update)
- [x] GCP billing-based enforcement triggered (POST / from real budget alert)
- [x] Flux estimator runs via Cloud Scheduler (GET /check-usage returns 200)
- [ ] Verify token-based estimator returns per-model cost breakdown
- [ ] Review all committed files for leaked credentials

Closes #2. Closes #4. Closes #5.

author: timcavazzotto
body:
## Causa raiz de cada falha anterior

**dom-to-image-more:** Serializa o DOM para SVG via `<foreignObject>`. CSS variables definidas em classes (`.poster.theme-verde { --p-bg: ... }`) não se propagam para o contexto SVG — a spec SVG não herda variáveis CSS do documento host. Resultado: vars caem no fallback, cores somem, página fica verde/branca.

**Clone + dom-to-image-more:** Mesmo problema de serialização SVG. Além disso, o clone estava com `visibility: hidden` durante a captura, resultando em imagem em branco.

**html-to-image tentativa 1:** `canvasWidth + canvasHeight + pixelRatio` juntos fazem a lib criar canvas de `canvasWidth × pixelRatio` (~15.000px) → crash de memória → erro ao exportar.

**html-to-image tentativa 2:** Também usa SVG `<foreignObject>` internamente. Ao tentar embutir as fontes Google no SVG, faz fetch das URLs `fonts.googleapis.com` → falha de CORS no endpoint CSS ou rede restrita → exceção na captura.

## Solução definitiva: html2canvas

`html2canvas` **não usa SVG**. Renderiza diretamente para canvas 2D:

- Lê `getComputedStyle()` em cada elemento → CSS variables **resolvidas pelo browser** antes da captura
- Usa fontes já carregadas via `document.fonts.ready` → sem fetch de fontes externas, **sem CORS**
- Captura a ×4.385 (A3, 3508px, 300 DPI) ou ×6.201 (A2, 4961px, 300 DPI)

## Estratégia de captura

1. Remove temporariamente `transform: scale(0.68)` do `.paper-sheet` para que o `.poster` renderize em tamanho real (800×1131px) — necessário porque html2canvas captura nas coordenadas de layout reais, não visuais
2. Overlay branco (`z-index: 9998`) cobre o flash visual durante os ~500ms de captura
3. Transform é restaurado em `finally`, garantindo recuperação mesmo em caso de erro
4. `console.log('[PDF Export]', {...})` imprime dimensões e scale para debug

## Como testar

1. Abra o configurador, escolha qualquer tema/idioma/tom
2. Clique "Baixar PDF alta resolução"
3. Aguarde o toast "Gerando PDF…" e a conclusão
4. Verifique no console: `[PDF Export] { paperSize, BASE_W, posterOffsetW, posterOffsetH, targetW, scale, bgColor }`
5. Abra o PDF — design deve ser fiel ao preview: grade proporcional, campos com linha, legenda correta, fontes DM Mono e Inter

author: copilot
body:
Spring Boot was silently falling back to `localhost:5432` when `DB_URL`/`DB_USER`/`DB_PASS` env vars were unset, causing connection refusal on any deployment targeting Supabase.

## `application.yml`
- **Removed all datasource defaults** — `DB_URL`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASS` are now required; app fails fast if unset rather than attempting `localhost:5432`
- **Added explicit `driver-class-name: org.postgresql.Driver`**
- **`ddl-auto`: `validate` → `none`** — Flyway owns the schema; Hibernate must not validate or modify it

```yaml
# Before — silently falls back to local postgres
datasource:
  url: ${DB_URL:jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/krishimitra}
  username: ${DB_USER:krishimitra}
  password: ${DB_PASS:krishimitra}
  
jpa:
  hibernate:
    ddl-auto: validate

# After — required env vars, explicit driver, Flyway owns schema
datasource:
  url: ${DB_URL}
  username: ${DB_USER}
  password: ${DB_PASS}
  driver-class-name: org.postgresql.Driver

jpa:
  hibernate:
    ddl-auto: none
```

## `DEPLOYMENT.md`
- Updated Supabase connection string to use the **Connection Pooler (port 6543)** instead of the direct connection (port 5432) — pooler is required for PaaS/serverless deployments
- Updated `DB_USER` format to `postgres.<ref>` (pooler username format)
- Added note clarifying why port 6543 must be used

author: copilot
body:
`RegionManager.GetOrCreate` unconditionally called `region.Start()`, spawning a background tick thread. Tests driving ticks manually via `region.Tick(0)` raced against that thread — if the background thread consumed the `AddEntity` command first, `entity.Position` remained at its zero default, `WorldService.MoveEntity` read `RegionId = 0`, found no region, and silently dropped the move command.

## Changes

- **`RegionManager`** — Added `autoStart` parameter (default `true`). `GetOrCreate` now conditionally starts the tick thread:
  ```csharp
  public RegionManager(ILoggerFactory loggerFactory, bool autoStart = true)
  ```
  Production callers are unaffected. Tests that manually drive `Tick()` pass `autoStart: false` to suppress the background thread entirely.

- **`WorldTopologyTests.MakeWorldService()`** — Passes `autoStart: false` so all `WorldService` topology tests are deterministic with no thread interference.

body:
🎯 **What:** The vulnerability fixed was insufficient input validation on the contact form in `index.html`.
⚠️ **Risk:** Without validation, the form was vulnerable to excessively large submissions (potential DoS/buffer overflow risks for processing scripts) and the submission of malicious or junk data.
🛡️ **Solution:** I implemented a robust, self-contained fix by:
1. Adding HTML5 attributes (`minlength`, `maxlength`, `pattern`) to enforce reasonable length limits and restrict the "name" field to valid characters.
2. Injecting a JavaScript script to trim whitespace from the name, email, and message fields upon submission, ensuring cleaner data is sent to the backend.

Pre-scaled the `QPixmap` images for `ExplosionAnimation` and `Shield` during their initialization (`__init__`) and stored them as instance attributes (`self.scaled_frames` and `self.scaled_shield`). The `draw` method now renders these pre-scaled images instead of continuously calculating the scaled dimensions on every frame.

🎯 **Why:**
In PyQt rendering loops, calling `QPixmap.scaled()` continuously inside the `draw` or `paintEvent` methods is a severe bottleneck. It significantly slows down rendering as it calculates the new dimensions on every frame. By caching the scaled images during initialization, we can avoid this performance hit entirely.

📊 **Impact:**
Reduces the overhead of `QPixmap.scaled` to 0 calls per frame during standard rendering. This will make the game run significantly smoother with fewer lag spikes when an explosion occurs or when a shield is rendered.

🔬 **Measurement:**
The performance improvement can be measured by monitoring CPU and rendering time before and after the change. In the game itself, rendering `ExplosionAnimation` or `Shield` will take significantly less CPU cycles on average.

author: diegosucaria
body:
## Summary

Fixes three production issues with browser-use:

- **Stop doesn't cancel browser-use** — Clicking stop or `/stop` set a flag but the running `browser_use_task` kept going for minutes. The MCP call was never aborted. Now: MCP manager tracks `AbortController`s for long-running calls (`browser_use_*` prefix), and `cancelActiveCalls()` aborts them immediately. Wired to `stopGeneration()` (UI button), `/stop` command handler, and the tool loop stop check.

- **Steps always showed "thinking"** — The step callback used `output.actions` (doesn't exist) instead of `output.action` (the actual `AgentOutput` field). All 20+ steps logged as "thinking" even when browser-use was clicking and typing. Now shows actual actions + next_goal:
  ```
  [browser-use] Step 3: click — Select 'Salta (SLA)' from suggestions | https://google.com/travel/flights
  ```

- **MCP SDK signal support** — `callTool` now passes `AbortSignal` to the MCP SDK, which sends `notifications/cancelled` to the server. FastMCP cancels the asyncio task, triggering the `finally` block that cleans up the browser.

## Cancellation flow
```
User clicks Stop → stopGeneration() → mcp.cancelActiveCalls()
  → AbortController.abort() → MCP SDK sends notifications/cancelled
  → FastMCP cancels asyncio task → CancelledError in browser_use_task
  → finally block: stop screencast + browser.stop()
```

## Test plan

- [x] All 460 tests pass
- [ ] Deploy, run browser_use_task, click Stop → verify it stops within seconds
- [ ] Verify step logs show actual actions (click, input, navigate) not just "thinking"
- [ ] Verify browser cleanup happens after cancel (no zombie Chrome processes)

*This section details on the original issue you should resolve*

<issue_title>[speckit.plan] Security Review</issue_title>
<issue_description>> **Parent Issue:** Boykai/github-workflows#5277 — Security Review

## 🤖 Agent Task: `speckit.plan`

Create a detailed implementation plan. Break down the specification into actionable steps, identify dependencies, and define the order of execution.

---

## Parent Issue Context

Plan: Security, Privacy & Vulnerability Audit
3 Critical · 8 High · 9 Medium · 2 Low — across OWASP Top 10. Findings describe the vulnerable pattern/behavior, not tied to specific function or line numbers.

Phase 1 — Critical (Fix Immediately)
1. Session token passed in URL — OWASP A02 (Critical)
The OAuth flow redirects the browser to the frontend with ?session_token=... in the URL. Tokens in URLs are recorded in browser history, server/proxy/CDN access logs, and HTTP Referer headers.

Correct behavior: Backend sets an HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Secure cookie directly on the OAuth callback response and redirects with no credentials in the URL. Frontend must never read credentials from URL params.
Files: auth.py, useAuth.ts
2. At-rest encryption not enforced — OWASP A02 (Critical)
ENCRYPTION_KEY is optional; when absent the app logs a warning and stores OAuth tokens in plaintext SQLite.

Correct behavior: On startup in non-debug mode, the application must refuse to start if ENCRYPTION_KEY is not set. Also apply the same mandatory rule to GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
Files: config.py, encryption.py
3. Frontend container runs as root — OWASP A05 (Critical)
The frontend Dockerfile has no USER directive; nginx runs as uid=0. The backend already runs non-root.

Correct behavior: All containers must run as a dedicated non-root system user.
Files: Dockerfile
Phase 2 — High (This Week)
4. Project resources not scoped to authenticated user — OWASP A01 (High)
Endpoints that accept a project_id (task creation, WebSocket subscription, project settings, workflow operations) do not verify the authenticated user owns that project. Any authenticated user can target any project by guessing its ID.

Correct behavior: Every endpoint accepting a project identifier must verify the session has access to that project before performing any action. Centralize this check as a shared dependency.
Files: tasks.py, projects.py, settings.py, workflow.py
5. Timing attack on Signal webhook — OWASP A07 (High)
Signal webhook secret comparison uses standard string equality (!=), which leaks timing information. The GitHub webhook already uses hmac.compare_digest correctly.

Correct behavior: All secret/token comparisons throughout the codebase must use constant-time comparison.
Files: signal.py
6. Missing HTTP security headers in nginx — OWASP A05 (High)
Only basic headers are set. Missing: Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy. The present X-XSS-Protection is deprecated in modern browsers.

Correct behavior: Add all five headers; remove X-XSS-Protection; set server_tokens off to hide nginx version.
Files: nginx.conf
7. Dev endpoint accepts GitHub PAT in URL — OWASP A02 (High)
The dev login endpoint receives a GitHub Personal Access Token as a URL query parameter.

Correct behavior: All credential inputs, even dev-only, must arrive in the POST request body (JSON), never in the URL.
Files: auth.py
8. OAuth requests overly broad repo scope — OWASP A01 (High)
The app requests the repo scope, which grants full read/write access to all private repositories. Only project management access is needed.

Correct behavior: Request minimum necessary scopes. Test that all write operations work with narrower scopes before removing repo.
Files: github_auth.py
9. Session secret key has no minimum entropy check — OWASP A07 (High)
SESSION_SECRET_KEY is accepted at any length with no validation.

Correct behavior: Startup must reject keys shorter than 64 characters.
Files: config.py
10. Docker services bound to all network interfaces — OWASP A05 (High)
Backend and frontend ports are bound to 0.0.0.0, exposing them on all interfaces.

Correct behavior: Development: bind to 127.0.0.1 only. Production: expose only via a reverse proxy, not directly via container ports.
Files: docker-compose.yml
Phase 3 — Medium (Next Sprint)
11. No rate limiting on expensive/sensitive endpoints — OWASP A04 (Medium)
Chat, agent invocation, workflow, and OAuth callback endpoints have no per-user or per-IP rate limits. A single user can exhaust shared AI/GitHub quotas.

Correct behavior: Per-user limits on write/AI endpoints; per-IP limit on OAuth callback. slowapi (FastAPI-compatible) is the recommended library.
Files: chat.py, agents.py, workflow.py, auth.py
12. Cookie Secure flag not enforced in production — OWASP A02 (Medium)
cookie_secure defaults to False and relies on indirect URL-prefix detection to enable it — fragile and silently misconfigures.

Correct behavior: Startup in non-debug mode must fail if cookie...

</details>

`BetaHuhn/repo-file-sync-action` was creating PRs in every target repo despite `PR: false` being set — a known limitation of that action on first-run/new-branch scenarios.

## Changes

- **`.github/workflows/sync-copilot-instructions.yml`** — Replaced entirely. Drops the third-party action in favor of a bash loop that clones each repo, copies the file, and pushes directly to `main`. Skips repos with no diff. Bumps `actions/checkout` to `v4`.
- **`.github/sync.yml`** — Deleted. Only existed to configure `BetaHuhn/repo-file-sync-action`.

## Result

```bash
for REPO in "${REPOS[@]}"; do
  git clone "https://x-access-token:${GH_PAT}@github.com/${REPO}.git" target-repo
  cp .github/copilot-instructions.md target-repo/.github/copilot-instructions.md
  cd target-repo
  git add .github/copilot-instructions.md
  if git diff --cached --quiet; then
    echo "No changes in $REPO, skipping."
  else
    git commit -m "chore: sync copilot-instructions.md from .github repo"
    git push  # direct to main — no PR
  fi
  cd .. && rm -rf target-repo
done
```

Covers all 30 Summit-Athletics repos. Requires `GH_PAT` secret with `repo` scope.

author: rogermt
body:
## Problem

After uploading a video and running a job, pressing "Run Job" again tried to re-upload the same video file instead of re-using the already uploaded video path. This caused:
- Wasted bandwidth
- Slower user experience
- Potential "Network error during upload" on consecutive uploads

## Solution

Store the uploaded `video_path` in local state and re-use it for consecutive job runs. Only upload when user selects a new file.

## Changes

**VideoUpload.tsx:**
- Added `videoPath` state to store uploaded video path
- Modified `handleRunJob` and `handleStartStreaming` to check videoPath first
- Skip upload if videoPath already set
- Clear videoPath when different file selected
- Show "Video uploaded ✓" status indicator

**VideoUpload.test.tsx (NEW):**
- Test: upload happens on first Run Job click
- Test: upload is SKIPPED on second Run Job click (re-use videoPath)
- Test: selecting different file clears videoPath and triggers new upload
- Test: "Video uploaded" status is shown after successful upload

## State Flow

```
Select File → file set, videoPath=null
Run Job #1 → Upload → videoPath="video/input/xxx.mp4"
Run Job #2 → Skip upload, use videoPath ✓
Select New File → Clear videoPath
Run Job #3 → Upload new file
```

## TEST-CHANGE JUSTIFICATION

Tests added to verify the new videoPath re-use behavior:
- Ensures upload is skipped on consecutive runs
- Ensures videoPath is cleared when different file selected
- Ensures "Video uploaded" status is displayed

Fixes #366

body:
## Summary

- **CSP blocking Sentry/BugSink**: `connect-src` in `proxy.ts` only allowed `*.sentry.io` — added `bugs.fullchaos.dev` (prod) and `localhost:8800` (local BugSink)
- **Added `tunnelRoute: "/monitoring"`** to `withSentryConfig` — proxies Sentry requests through the Next.js server, bypassing CSP and DNS resolution issues entirely
- **Static-export CSP fallback** in `next.config.js` was also missing Sentry domains — added `*.sentry.io` and `bugs.fullchaos.dev`

## Root cause

Client-side Sentry was silently failing because:
1. The SDK reads `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` (requires `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix for client-side bundling), but only `SENTRY_DSN` was set in env
2. CSP `connect-src` blocked the BugSink domain
3. No Sentry tunnel was configured to bypass CSP

## Deploy notes

Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` in the web service environment (same value as existing `SENTRY_DSN`):
```
NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN=https://48607ebfef6c41f9bb6572a6a6dee58d@bugs.fullchaos.dev/1
```

The `compose.yml` at the repo root (not in this git repo) also needs:
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN: ${NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN:-}` in the web service environment
- `logging.service.name` / `logging.service.namespace` Docker labels on all services for OTEL collector log discovery

TEST-WAIVER: CSP and config-only changes — no component logic affected

Potential fix for [https://github.com/Ndevu12/the_inventory/security/code-scanning/1](https://github.com/Ndevu12/the_inventory/security/code-scanning/1)

In general, you should explicitly declare a `permissions` block in the workflow (or per job) so the GITHUB_TOKEN has only the scopes it needs. For this CI job, it only needs to read repository contents to allow `actions/checkout` to work, so `contents: read` at the workflow or job level is sufficient.

The best minimal fix without changing existing functionality is to add a workflow-level `permissions` block near the top of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, so it applies to all current and future jobs that don’t override it. Specifically, insert:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
```

between the `name: CI` and the `on:` sections (around line 2–3). No imports or additional methods are needed, since this is a pure YAML configuration change. This will limit the GITHUB_TOKEN to read-only access to repository contents, which is enough for `actions/checkout@v4` and does not interfere with any of the Python/Django commands that run locally.

author: yunchuwang
body:
Fixes #190

## Problem
setCustomStatus() stores the raw object without serialization, and getCustomStatus() calls JSON.stringify() lazily. The problem is that getCustomStatus() is called outside the executor's try-catch block, so if a user passes a non-serializable value (e.g., circular references, BigInt), the orchestration result is completely lost.

## Changes
- Serialize eagerly in setCustomStatus() so serialization errors are thrown inside orchestrator code (within the executor's try-catch)
- Store the pre-serialized JSON string so getCustomStatus() becomes a trivial getter that cannot throw
- Ensures the orchestration properly fails with a descriptive error rather than silently losing results

In general, this should be fixed by adding an explicit `permissions:` block that grants the least privileges required by this workflow and the reusable workflows it calls. For CI tasks that only read repository content and do not push commits, releases, or other write operations, `contents: read` is typically sufficient and is the recommended minimal baseline.

In this specific file, the simplest and safest fix without changing existing functionality is to add a top-level `permissions:` block after the `on:` declaration. This root-level block will apply to all jobs in this workflow (unless a job or called reusable workflow explicitly overrides permissions). Given the names and nature of the jobs (`pre-commit`, `phan`, `phpstan`, `windows-ci`), they are classic read-only CI checks, so `contents: read` is an appropriate minimal setting. No other files or imports are involved, and no job definitions need to be altered.

Concretely, in `.github/workflows/ci-on-push.yml`, insert:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
```

between the `on: [push]` line and the `jobs:` block.

author: nagarenegishi
body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive production deployment pipeline and several important security and configuration improvements. The main changes include adding a GitHub Actions workflow for automated CI/CD, updating Docker Compose to use pre-built images from ECR, tightening production environment settings, and enhancing security headers in the Nginx configuration.

**CI/CD Pipeline and Deployment:**

* Added a new `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` GitHub Actions workflow to automate testing, building, pushing Docker images to AWS ECR, running database migrations, and deploying the application to EC2. This workflow ensures a robust, automated path from code to production.

**Docker and Deployment Configuration:**

* Updated `compose.prod.yml` to pull pre-built `nginx` and `backend` images from ECR instead of building them on the EC2 host, streamlining deployments and ensuring consistency with CI builds. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3c22f73b491d3a17d8206e1d06eb996298a8640f24a5b5db28f8d961f9c6771bL4-R7) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3c22f73b491d3a17d8206e1d06eb996298a8640f24a5b5db28f8d961f9c6771bL15-R17)

**Production Environment Hardening:**

* Set `AllowedHosts` in `JobTrackerApi/appsettings.Production.json` to the production domain (`jobtracker.nagarenegishi.com`) instead of allowing all hosts, reducing the risk of host header attacks.

**Security Improvements:**

* Enhanced `job-tracker-ui/nginx.conf` with a comprehensive set of HTTP security headers, including Content Security Policy (CSP), HSTS (instructions), X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and X-Content-Type-Options, significantly improving frontend security and resilience against common web attacks.

body:
# Pull Request #51 — Description

## Title
Implement `Job#perform` to execute resource requests

## Summary
This PR introduces the `Job#perform` method, which is responsible for executing HTTP requests based on the associated `ResourceRequest`. To enable this functionality, the `Job` class was refactored to receive a `ClientRegistry` instance during construction, allowing it to resolve the appropriate client for the request.

## Changes
- **`Job` class:**
  - Added the `#perform` method, which retrieves the correct client from the `ClientRegistry` and executes the `ResourceRequest`.
  - Refactored the constructor to accept a `clients` parameter (an instance of `ClientRegistry`).
  - Introduced the private `#getClient` method to resolve the client based on the `clientName` specified in the `ResourceRequest`.

## Implementation Details
- The `Job#perform` method:
  - Uses the `ClientRegistry` to retrieve the client associated with the `ResourceRequest`'s `clientName`.
  - Executes the `perform` method of the resolved client, passing the `ResourceRequest`.

## Next Steps
Future PRs will focus on:
1. Improving test coverage for `Job#perform`.
2. Ensuring that the `ResourceRequest` correctly provides the `clientName` for client resolution.
3. Handling and processing the response from the HTTP request, including error handling and downstream job creation.

## Checklist
- [x] Added `Job#perform` to execute resource requests.
- [x] Refactored `Job` to accept `ClientRegistry` in its constructor.
- [x] Introduced `#getClient` for client resolution.
- [ ] Improve test coverage for `Job#perform` (planned for future PRs).
- [ ] Handle `ResourceRequest` response processing (planned for future PRs).

## How to Test
1. Create a `Job` instance with a `ResourceRequest` and a `ClientRegistry`.
2. Call `job.perform()` and verify that the correct client is used to execute the request.

## Notes
This PR lays the groundwork for the `Job` execution flow. While the basic functionality is in place, additional work is required to handle responses and improve test coverage.

Introduced Day 11 of the 30 Days of OpenTofu curriculum, focusing on Managed Identities and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) in Azure. This lab demonstrates how to securely grant permissions to a service without using long-lived secrets or passwords.

### List of Changes
- **Infrastructure:** Created `day-11/` directory for the Identity and RBAC laboratory.
- **Identity:** Provisioned an `azurerm_user_assigned_identity` named `id-app-reader`.
- **Resources:** Created an `azurerm_storage_account` to serve as the target for permission testing.
- **RBAC:** Implemented an `azurerm_role_assignment` to grant the `Storage Blob Data Reader` role to the Managed Identity at the specific Storage Account scope.
- **Compliance:** Followed the "Principle of Least Privilege" by scoping the role assignment to a specific resource rather than the entire resource group or subscription.
- **Documentation:** Authored `day-11/README.md` covering Managed Identity benefits and the three components of RBAC (Principal, Role, Scope).

### Verification
- [x] Verified `tofu validate` confirms correct configuration of identity and role assignment.
- [x] Confirmed `tofu plan` shows the role assignment correctly targeting the Storage Account resource ID.
- [x] Validated that the Managed Identity principal ID is dynamically passed to the role assignment resource.

body:
🛡️ Sentinel: Harden Cloud API CORS and Security Headers

This commit implements a high-impact security enhancement for the Cloud API (FastAPI) to prevent common browser-based vulnerabilities.

Key Changes:
- Sets `allow_credentials=False` in `CORSMiddleware` to align with the `allow_origins=["*"]` wildcard, preventing potential CSRF and credential leakage.
- Adds a global middleware to enforce defense-in-depth security headers:
    - `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` (Prevents MIME sniffing)
    - `X-Frame-Options: DENY` (Prevents Clickjacking)
    - `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'` (Strict source control)

These changes follow security best practices and have been verified with both unit tests and `bandit` security scans.

author: garretfick
body:
## Summary

- Fix the named-to-positional argument transform to register `REF_TO ARRAY[...] OF T` parameters in function signatures using the element type name, instead of skipping them
- Update the `end_to_end_when_function_with_deref_array_subscript_then_writes_through_ref` test to verify full runtime execution (write through REF and read back)

## Details

The test was compile-only because calling a function with a `REF_TO ARRAY` parameter caused a `StackUnderflow` at runtime. The root cause was in `xform_resolve_symbol_and_function_environment.rs`: inline array reference targets (`REF_TO ARRAY[0..10] OF BYTE`) returned `None` from `type_name()`, so the parameter was skipped with `continue`. This left the function signature with zero parameters, causing `xform_named_to_positional_args` to produce zero positional arguments. At runtime, CALL tried to pop the missing argument from an empty stack.

The VM's `STORE_ARRAY_DEREF` / `LOAD_ARRAY_DEREF` opcodes and the codegen for `PT^[idx]` were already fully implemented — only the analyzer transform needed fixing.

## Test plan

- [x] `end_to_end_when_function_with_deref_array_subscript_then_writes_through_ref` now runs through the VM and verifies `arr[0] == 42` after writing through the reference
- [x] All workspace tests pass
- [x] Clippy clean, formatting clean

author: stasson
body:
## Summary

- Standardize internal structure of all 40 domain files with `## Standard`, `## Regulation`, `## Publication` sections
- Add `Label:` and `Keywords:` metadata to all 613 entries (483 Standard / 60 Regulation / 70 Publication)
- Add domain description and Contents TOC to each file
- Rename 5 files for clarity: acoustics, artificial-intelligence, electromagnetic-compatibility, graphics-rendering, telecommunications
- Merge cybersecurity + privacy → cybersecurity-privacy (ISO 27000 series covers both)
- Update AGENTS.md conventions and README.md domain table with full linked list

## Motivation

Registry files had inconsistent internal organization — some used topic sections, some had a `## Regulation` section, some were flat. Contributors lacked clear guidance on where to add entries. Research into ICS, ACM CCS, and ISO bibliographic standards confirmed domain-first organization is correct, but a type-based split (Standard/Regulation/Publication) inside each file adds real value for navigation and classification.

## Classification rules

- **Standard** — normative technical specifications (ISO, IEC, IEEE, SAE, RFCs, consortium specs)
- **Regulation** — legally binding (EU directives, UN regulations, national laws)
- **Publication** — everything else (NIST SPs, OWASP, frameworks, guides, books)

## Problem

## Why
The scheduled acceptance smoke started failing on Arbitrum Sepolia because the demo script hard-coded `USDC` as the collateral token for `ETH/USDC:USDC`, while the live GMX market metadata now reports `USDC.SG` as the valid short-side collateral token. That mismatch causes the bridge order parser to fail with `Not a valid collateral for selected market!`.

author: wireworks-operations
body:
### 💡 What: The optimization implemented
This PR implements search debouncing and refactors the filtering logic to be more efficient.

1.  **Search Debouncing**: Introduced a `debounce` utility and applied it to the search input's `input` event with a 150ms delay.
2.  **Single-Pass Refactor**: Consolidated filtering and result counting into a single loop in `searchResults` and `filterCategory`, removing the need for a separate `updateResultCount` pass.
3.  **Immediate 'Enter' Response**: The 'Enter' key now triggers an immediate search while canceling any pending debounced calls.

### 🎯 Why: The performance problem it solves
Previously, the application would:
- Iterate through all results twice on every search/filter action (once for display, once for counting).
- Re-run the entire search/filter logic on EVERY keystroke, leading to redundant DOM updates and potential layout thrashing during rapid typing.

### 📊 Impact: Expected performance improvement
- **Calls Reduction**: Reduces the number of `searchResults` executions by ~85% during typical typing speeds (e.g., 8 calls reduced to 1 for a 7-letter word).
- **Algorithmic Efficiency**: Reduces filtering/counting complexity from $O(2N)$ to $O(N)$ per execution.
- **Improved UX**: Typing feels smoother on slower devices, while the 'Enter' key remains instantaneous.

### 🔬 Measurement: How to verify the improvement
The improvement was verified using a Playwright script that injected a call counter into the window. For a 7-character input ('systems'), the call count dropped from 8 to 1. Result counts and category filtering were also verified to remain accurate.

### ⚡ Bolt's Journal Update
Updated `.Jules/bolt.md` with learnings regarding debouncing and single-pass iteration patterns in single-page applications.

body:
## Summary

Adds an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server to shep, enabling external AI agents (Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, Windsurf, etc.) to discover and invoke shep capabilities as MCP tools over stdio transport.

- **New `shep mcp` CLI command** — launches a foreground MCP server on stdio (stdin/stdout JSON-RPC), with `--log-level` option and Claude Desktop config example in `--help`
- **11 MCP tools** exposing core use cases: `list_features`, `show_feature`, `create_feature`, `start_feature`, `run_agent`, `show_agent_run`, `list_agent_runs`, `stop_agent_run`, `list_repositories`, `get_settings`, `update_settings`
- **Thin presentation adapter** — each tool handler resolves its use case from the shared DI container, with zod-validated input schemas and structured error responses (`isError: true`)
- **Stdio safety** — zero `console.log` calls in MCP code; all diagnostics go to stderr only
- **Graceful shutdown** — handles SIGINT/SIGTERM to cleanly close the MCP transport

### Architecture

The MCP server follows the existing Clean Architecture pattern as a new presentation adapter:

```
presentation/cli/commands/mcp.command.ts  →  DI container  →  McpServerService
                                                                  ├── feature tools
                                                                  ├── agent tools
                                                                  ├── repository tools
                                                                  └── settings tools
```

Uses `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` v1.27.1 with native zod v4 support. Server identifies as "shep" with the current CLI version. Long-running operations (agent runs) return immediately with a run ID.

## Evidence

- **75 unit tests** across 7 test files (server service, DI registration, feature/agent/repo/settings tools, CLI command) — all passing
- **23 integration tests** using `InMemoryTransport` + MCP `Client` for protocol round-trip verification (initialize, tools/list, tools/call success/error paths, input validation, server resilience) — all passing
- **Full test suite**: 4824 unit tests (355 files) + 569 integration tests (48 files) = 5393 tests — zero failures
- **Build + lint**: `pnpm build` and `pnpm lint` (eslint --max-warnings 0) both pass with zero errors
- **Stdio safety**: grep confirms zero `console.log` calls in MCP server code

### Motivation
- Fix the §11 bug where the sandwich construction stored a product-of-totals instead of the paper-intended sum-of-sandwiches `∑_a A_a (∑_b B_b) A_a` and make the intent explicit. 
- Enforce the §12 interpolation threshold from the paper by requiring at least `d+1` genuine polynomial slices before producing a global interpolant.

### Description
- Rewrote `sandwichByOuterSubMeasurement.totalOperator` so it computes the sum-of-sandwiches over `a` using `sumOperatorList` when a `Fintype α` instance is available, and added a documented fallback placeholder for the non-finite case (`MIPStarRE/Paper2009LDT/Section11Commutativity.lean`).
- Added `nonBottomSliceCount` to count non-`⊥` entries and changed `interpolateCompletedSlices` to check `params.d + 1 ≤ nonBottomSliceCount gs` before attempting interpolation, returning the fallback polynomial otherwise (`MIPStarRE/Paper2009LDT/Section12Pasting.lean`).
- Updated TODO comments in §11/§12 to record the finite/non-finite mismatch and that the current preliminary formalization still uses a first-available-slice stand-in rather than full polynomial interpolation.

### Testing
- Ran `lake build MIPStarRE.Paper2009LDT` and the build completed successfully. 
- The build emitted unrelated repository warnings and existing `sorry` placeholders, but the changes in `Section11Commutativity.lean` and `Section12Pasting.lean` did not cause failures.

author: alexk-dev
body:
## Summary

Extracts the monolithic `ContextBuildingSystem` (742 lines, 16 dependencies, 8 tangled concerns) into a composable, layered context assembly architecture inspired by Google Antigravity's context engineering patterns.

**Key changes:**

- **New `domain/context` package** with clean orchestration abstractions:
  - `ContextLayer` interface — contract for composable context sections with ordering, applicability checks, and assembly
  - `ContextLayerResult` — immutable result of layer assembly (content + token estimate + metadata)
  - `ContextBlueprint` — ordered collection of layer results, acts as diagnostic artifact and input to prompt composition
  - `ContextAssembler` — main orchestrator running a 4-phase pipeline: skill resolution → tier resolution → layer assembly → prompt composition
  - `PromptComposer` — joins layer content into the final system prompt
  - `SkillResolver` / `TierResolver` — extracted resolution logic with clear priority chains

- **10 independent context layers**, each isolated and self-documenting:
  - `IdentityLayer` (10), `WorkspaceInstructionsLayer` (20), `MemoryLayer` (30), `RagLayer` (35), `SkillLayer` (40), `ToolLayer` (50), `TierAwarenessLayer` (60), `AutoModeLayer` (70), `PlanModeLayer` (72), `HiveLayer` (75)

- **`ContextBuildingSystem` reduced to 17 lines** — now a thin delegate to `ContextAssembler`

- **Progressive disclosure** for skills: full active skill content loaded on demand, inactive skills shown as summaries only

- **80 new tests** across 14 test files, developed TDD-first. All 3101 tests pass.

- **All new classes have detailed Javadoc** documenting purpose, order ranges, and design rationale

## Summary

- Hyphens in address fields are now replaced with a space before matching, rather than silently removed
- Applies to both `normalise_address` (Python) and `_NORMALISE_MACRO` (DuckDB, used in tiers 2 and 3)
- Non-hyphen punctuation (apostrophes, periods) behaviour unchanged

## Why

`[^\w\s]` previously stripped hyphens silently, turning `CROSS-O-THE-HANDS` → `CROSSOTHEHANDS`. The same address written with spaces in the other source (`CROSS O THE HANDS`) no longer matched. Measured gain on March 2026 cache: **+2,428 matched records**.
